title: How much hand-coding can an LLM coder replace, with a valid interval, when its error differs by group and the category is rare?
lede: research programme: valid inference from LLM-coded qualitative data under group shift and rare categories; estimator library built, and the stratified normal interval covers only 57% at 1% prevalence (83% at 3%) in simulation
summary: An open research programme. A stdlib estimator library is built and tested. First preliminary result, on simulated corpora with a stand-in coder: the normal interval of a coder-label-stratified audit covers 57% at 1% prevalence, 83% at 3% and 94% at 20% (nominal 95%), so rare-category audit designs need small-count-safe intervals. An LLM's codes for qualitative text carry error that can differ between groups, and prediction-powered inference corrects counts, gaps and coefficients from a random hand-coded audit. The earlier qual-* projects showed on GoEmotions, with stand-in coders and no LLM, that naive counts are confidently wrong, that the correction is valid but wider than hand-coding alone for weak coders, and that a random audit cannot estimate a rare group. The programme asks when the audit can be small and how to sample it when the coder's error differs by group and the target category has prevalence under 5%. Hypotheses H1 to H5 cover pooled-correction failure under group shift, the end of the gain for rare categories, a real LLM coder, audit design, and a closed-form audit-size rule. Limits at this stage: the proposal's references were written from memory because the arXiv and Crossref hosts were blocked, and are to be machine-checked in milestone 1.
